steps.name: Condition x time interaction LRT

Shrinkage with apeglm requires a coefficient name, not a contrast vector; use the coefficient form or fall back to ashr and say which was used
steps.context: This is the step that answers the research question directly. The shared time trend and the constant baseline offset between conditions are both absorbed by the reduced model, so the LRT isolates genes whose temporal trajectory differs by treatment. An omnibus interaction p-value says trajectories differ but not how, so the step also extracts the three interaction contrasts (condition:t1, condition:t2, condition:t3, each relative to t0) to localize the divergence in time.
steps.question: Which genes show a treatment-specific change across t0..t3 — i.e. which genes have a significant condition:time interaction beyond the time trend shared by both arms — and at which time points does the treated-vs-control difference emerge?
constraints: The reduced model must be ~condition + time — it must retain the condition main effect, so a constant baseline shift between arms is NOT reported as treatment-specific
Use test="LRT" with the reduced formula; do not substitute a per-timepoint Wald contrast as the primary answer to the research question
Apply independent filtering as DESeq2 defaults do and report the filtering threshold used
Report FDR-adjusted p-values (BH) as the primary significance criterion; never report raw p-value counts as the headline
Use the DESeqDataSet built in T1S1 without rebuilding the design differently
steps.description: Run DESeq2 with a likelihood-ratio test comparing full design ~condition + time + condition:time against reduced ~condition + time, producing a per-gene omnibus interaction statistic (3 df). Report the full results table (baseMean, LRT stat, pvalue, padj) sorted by padj, the number of genes at FDR < 0.05 and < 0.10, and for the significant set extract each individual interaction coefficient (condition x t1, t2, t3 vs t0) with shrunken log2 fold changes. Also run, for reference and contrast, the main-effect time LRT (~condition + time vs ~condition) so the size of the shared time response can be compared against the treatment-specific one. acceptance_criteria: Full and reduced model formulas printed verbatim in the output alongside resultsNames() so the coefficient naming is unambiguous
Interaction LRT results table for all tested genes written to CSV with columns: gene, baseMean, stat, pvalue, padj, plus the three interaction log2FC estimates

steps.name: Cluster interaction genes into temporal response patterns
caveats: With 4 time points a trajectory has only 4 points — do not over-partition; more than ~6 clusters is not interpretable at this resolution

steps.context: A ranked interaction gene list does not communicate the biology of a time course. steps.question: Among the genes with a significant condition:time interaction, what distinct shapes does the treated-minus-control difference take across t0..t3 — early transient, late sustained, progressive, or opposing — and how many genes fall into each?
constraints: Cluster on the treated-minus-control difference trajectory, not on raw expression — clustering raw expression recovers the shared time trend, which is exactly what the question excludes

acceptance_criteria: Significance threshold used for the input gene set stated explicitly, with the resulting gene count
Number of clusters chosen by a stated criterion (silhouette, elbow, or dendrogram cut height) rather than picked arbitrarily
Clustered heatmap of treated-minus-control VST trajectories across t0..t3 saved, annotated by cluster
Cluster-mean trajectory plot saved with the number of genes per cluster labelled

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treatment-specific temporal programmes
caveats: The matrix holds 12,000 genes, likely a pre-filtered subset rather than the full transcriptome; this truncated universe biases enrichment and must be acknowledged
GO BP sets are hierarchically nested, so significant hits come in correlated blocks — collapse redundant parent/child terms before reporting a count
If the T1S3 clusters are small (tens of genes), over-representation will be underpowered; report set sizes alongside p-values
steps.context: Takes the interaction LRT ranking from T1S2 and the cluster assignments from T1S3 and annotates them functionally. Needs human gene-set collections keyed on HGNC symbols — the counts matrix is already indexed by gene symbol, so no ID conversion should be needed beyond checking symbol overlap with the gene-set universe. Human hallmark and GO biological-process collections, and human WikiPathways, are present in this environment; the executing agent must resolve them at run time and must use the human (not mouse or rat) versions.
steps.question: Which biological processes and hallmark states are enriched among the condition x time interaction genes overall, and which are specific to each temporal response cluster?
constraints: Background universe for over-representation must be the genes actually tested in T1S2 after filtering, not all annotated human genes
Use human gene sets only — the mouse and rat collections in this environment are for other organisms and would produce meaningless overlap
Report FDR-adjusted significance; do not present nominal p-values as the headline result
Do not interpret enrichment of a cluster as mechanism — these are cell-line expression responses, and the write-up must say so

GSEA results table (set, size, NES, pvalue, padj, leading-edge genes) written to CSV for hallmark and GO BP
Over-representation results per temporal cluster written to CSV, using the T1S2 tested-gene set as the background universe — not the whole genome
Ranking metric for GSEA stated explicitly, including how the unsigned LRT statistic was given a direction
Significant sets reported at FDR < 0.05 with a plot (dot plot or bar plot) per collection; if none are significant this is stated plainly rather than backfilled with nominal p-values

plan.title: Treatment x time interaction DE in 2x4 time course
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 25-column raw salmon count matrix (counts.csv; first column is the gene symbol, so 24 sample columns) with a 24-row metadata table carrying condition, time (t0..t3) and time_hours — a 2-condition x 4-timepoint design with 3 replicates per cell. The research question ('genes with a treatment-specific change over time, beyond the shared time trend') is exactly a condition x time interaction test, so the plan is built around a DESeq2 likelihood-ratio test of ~condition + time + condition:time against the reduced model ~condition + time. That reduced model absorbs the time trend shared by both arms and the constant baseline offset between arms, leaving only genes whose trajectory shape differs by treatment.

T1S1 builds the DESeq2 object with time as a 4-level factor (not a continuous covariate: with only four unequally-informative points a factor model makes no functional-form assumption and, at n=24 with 12,000 genes, uses only 3 extra df) and runs QC — library sizes, VST PCA coloured by condition and time, sample distance clustering — to check that time is the dominant axis and that no replicate is an outlier before any inference. It also verifies that the 24 metadata rows match the 24 count columns and that condition/time are not confounded.

T1S2 runs the interaction LRT itself and, because an omnibus LRT tells you that trajectories differ but not how, extracts the per-timepoint treated-vs-control contrasts (t1, t2, t3 each relative to t0) with shrunken effect sizes so each interaction gene can be described by where and when it diverges. T1S3 clusters the significant interaction genes on their condition-difference trajectories, turning a gene list into a small number of temporal response patterns (early transient, late sustained, opposing) and reporting each cluster's membership. T2S1 takes those clusters plus the LRT ranking to hallmark and GO BP enrichment against the staged human MSigDB GMTs, so the temporal patterns get a biological read-out.

Caveats carried into the steps: 3 replicates per cell is the minimum for a per-cell dispersion-informed interaction test, the interaction LRT is the least-powered contrast in this design, and salmon counts are non-integer in general — the profile states they are raw integer counts, but the step must confirm and round rather than assume. 12,000 x 24 is tiny (a few MB), so resources stay small throughout.
